dependencies.name: @emotion/cache
dependencies.purpose: Provides the deterministic Emotion cache used by the official MUI App Router server-rendering integration.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns cache placement and hydration invariants; Emotion owns style serialization and cache mechanics.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Consumed only by the MUI Next.js integration at the root application boundary, not by business screens.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace only with the paired MUI styling-engine or framework integration while preserving head-managed SSR style and hydration proof.

maturity.rationale: Stable official Emotion cache package required by MUI's documented Next.js App Router integration.

dependencies.name: @emotion/react
dependencies.purpose: Provides the React styling runtime required by the governed MUI component foundation.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns its MUI theme and component usage; Emotion owns the styling engine implementation.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Consumed as an MUI peer runtime behind the Workbench design-system theme and component boundary.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace only through an issue-backed MUI styling-engine migration with visual and accessibility regression proof.

maturity.rationale: Established styling runtime used by MUI with stable package documentation and an active public maintenance channel.

dependencies.name: @emotion/styled
dependencies.purpose: Provides the styled-component primitive required by the governed MUI styling engine.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns design tokens and composed components; Emotion owns styled-component runtime behavior.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Consumed as an MUI peer runtime behind the Workbench design-system theme and component boundary.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace only with the paired Emotion and MUI migration, including theme, rendering, and accessibility proof.

maturity.rationale: Established MUI-compatible styling primitive with stable documentation and a shared active Emotion maintenance channel.

dependencies.name: @hookform/resolvers
dependencies.purpose: Connects governed Zod validation to React Hook Form in the proposal simulation workflow.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns form rules and schemas; the adapter owns translation into React Hook Form results.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Imported only by the proposal simulation form and paired with repository-owned Zod schemas.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace with a repository-owned resolver adapter or direct validation at the proposal form boundary.

maturity.rationale: Official React Hook Form resolver collection with stable Zod integration and active public releases.

dependencies.name: @mui/material
dependencies.purpose: Provides accessible interaction primitives and theme integration for the Workbench design system.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns business composition, tokens, density, and interaction policy; MUI owns low-level primitives.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Business screens consume repository-owned design-system components; direct use is governed and reviewed.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Migrate through the Workbench design-system facade screen by screen with accessibility and visual-regression proof.

maturity.rationale: Long-lived, documented React component foundation with active releases, accessibility guidance, and enterprise usage patterns.

dependencies.name: @mui/material-nextjs
dependencies.purpose: Collects MUI and Emotion styles during Next.js App Router streaming so server-rendered styles are managed in the document head.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns root-provider composition and browser proof; MUI owns the supported Next.js cache-provider adapter.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Imported once by the root App Router layout and kept outside feature and business composition modules.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace only with MUI's supported successor or a reviewed repository adapter that proves identical SSR style placement and hydration behavior.

maturity.rationale: Official stable MUI adapter for long-lived Next.js App Router server rendering, version-compatible with the governed Next 15, React 19, and MUI 7 foundation.

dependencies.name: @noble/hashes
dependencies.purpose: Produces exact SHA-256 presentation-evidence digests when the governed HTTP runtime cannot expose secure-context Web Crypto digest APIs.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns the ordered candidate-set contract and digest label; noble-hashes owns the standards-compliant SHA-256 implementation.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Imported only by the Idea presentation receipt contract module as a fallback behind native Web Crypto.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Remove the fallback after the governed Workbench runtime is HTTPS-only and canonical browser proof confirms native Web Crypto on every supported origin.

maturity.rationale: Small tree-shakeable SHA-256 implementation with no runtime dependencies, public security guidance, independent audit evidence, test-vector coverage, and supported 2.x maintenance.

dependencies.name: @tanstack/react-query
dependencies.purpose: Coordinates bounded server-state retrieval, mutation, invalidation, and source refresh for Workbench workflows.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns query keys and truth-refresh rules; Gateway and source services own business state and persistence.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: A single provider and feature-owned hooks contain caching and mutation policy away from presentation components.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace through feature query hooks while retaining Gateway contracts, source refresh, and explicit failure semantics.

maturity.rationale: Established server-state library with versioned documentation, active releases, and framework-specific production guidance.

dependencies.name: ag-grid-community
dependencies.purpose: Provides dense, accessible, virtualized portfolio record grids for advisor holdings and transaction workflows.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns column semantics, formatting, and actions; AG Grid owns grid rendering and interaction mechanics.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Registration and behavior are contained in design-system grid utilities and portfolio record grid frames.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace behind the portfolio data-grid frame while preserving columns, keyboard behavior, density, and record actions.

maturity.rationale: Established data-grid product with a documented community edition, active releases, and mature enterprise interaction patterns.

dependencies.name: ag-grid-react
dependencies.purpose: Provides the React binding for governed AG Grid portfolio record surfaces.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns React composition and record behavior; the adapter owns React-to-grid lifecycle integration.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Imported only by repository-owned portfolio and positions grid-frame components.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace together with AG Grid Community behind the existing portfolio data-grid frame and module boundary.

maturity.rationale: Official React integration maintained and released with the established AG Grid community runtime.

dependencies.name: echarts
dependencies.purpose: Renders dense interactive performance, attribution, and risk visualizations from Workbench-owned chart models.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns financial labels and chart models; Apache ECharts owns rendering and chart interaction mechanics.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Chart options and rendering are contained by the repository-owned WorkbenchECharts design-system component.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace the renderer behind WorkbenchECharts while retaining source-owned data, chart models, labels, and disclosure rules.

maturity.rationale: Apache-governed visualization project with stable releases, broad chart coverage, and documented accessibility controls.

dependencies.name: echarts-for-react
dependencies.purpose: Provides the React lifecycle adapter used by the repository-owned WorkbenchECharts chart boundary.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns chart configuration and the facade; the adapter owns React mounting and ECharts lifecycle calls.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Imported only by WorkbenchECharts, preventing chart-adapter behavior from leaking across business screens.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace with a small repository-owned React adapter or another maintained binding behind WorkbenchECharts.

maturity.rationale: Long-lived focused React binding with a stable API, current releases, and narrow containment behind one local facade.

dependencies.name: next
dependencies.purpose: Provides the governed application framework, server rendering, routing, BFF endpoints, and standalone runtime packaging.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns product routes and BFF policy; Next.js owns framework execution, rendering, and packaging behavior.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Framework behavior is governed through App Router entrypoints, BFF routes, runtime policy, and standalone container proof.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Require an architecture RFC and staged migration preserving Gateway boundaries, routes, server behavior, and browser evidence.

maturity.rationale: Widely deployed React application framework with a published support policy, stable release channel, and mature self-hosting guidance.

dependencies.name: react
dependencies.purpose: Provides the component, state, and rendering model for every interactive Workbench business surface.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns components and business interaction state; React owns component lifecycle and reconciliation behavior.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Use is governed by feature boundaries, repository design-system components, strict TypeScript, and React lint controls.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Require an architecture RFC and product-wide staged rewrite preserving accessibility, BFF boundaries, and workflow evidence.

maturity.rationale: Long-lived, widely deployed UI foundation with stable documentation, active security maintenance, and extensive tooling support.

dependencies.name: react-dom
dependencies.purpose: Provides the browser and server DOM renderer paired with the governed React application runtime.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns application composition; React maintainers own DOM rendering and hydration behavior.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Consumed through the Next.js and React runtime rather than application-owned rendering infrastructure.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace only as part of the coordinated React and Next.js architecture migration path.

maturity.rationale: Official DOM renderer released and maintained with React, with stable integration through the selected Next.js framework.

dependencies.name: react-hook-form
dependencies.purpose: Manages accessible form state and validation flow for proposal simulation inputs.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns fields, business validation, and submission; React Hook Form owns local form-state coordination.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Imported only by the proposal simulation form and paired with repository-owned contracts and actions.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace within the proposal form boundary using React state or another reviewed form-state adapter.

maturity.rationale: Established React form-state library with stable documentation, active releases, and a focused browser-only responsibility.

dependencies.name: zod
dependencies.purpose: Validates external and form contracts at Workbench boundaries before business UI consumes them.
dependencies.ownershipBoundary: Workbench owns schemas and failure posture; Zod owns deterministic runtime parsing and validation mechanics.
dependencies.containmentBoundary: Schemas live in feature contract modules and proposal form validation rather than presentation components.

replacementPosture.exitPath: Replace contract modules incrementally with generated or repository-owned validators while preserving failure semantics.

maturity.rationale: Established TypeScript-first validation library with stable documentation, active releases, and contained contract-boundary usage.
